records.definition: An application programming interface that lets software systems exchange requests and data through defined rules.
Answer engine optimization: structuring useful information so answer-oriented search experiences can interpret and surface it.
A software system that can interpret a goal, choose from permitted actions, and carry out a multi-step task within defined boundaries.
A trained computational system that identifies patterns in input and produces outputs such as classifications, predictions, text, or recommendations.
A configured process that carries out defined actions when specified events or conditions occur.
A link from one website to another; relevant, trustworthy links can help people discover content and may support search authority.
The preferred URL specified for a page when similar or duplicate versions exist.
Continuous integration and continuous delivery or deployment: practices for testing, packaging, and releasing software in repeatable stages.
On-demand access to computing resources such as servers, storage, databases, and managed services over a network.
The proportion of visitors or users who complete a defined action, calculated against the relevant population.
Customer relationship management: tools and processes for organizing customer details, interactions, sales activity, and follow-up.
A sequence of steps that collects, transforms, validates, and moves data between sources and destinations.
A set of practices that improves collaboration between software development and operations, often through automation and shared responsibility.
Enterprise resource planning: connected software for managing core business operations such as finance, inventory, purchasing, and planning.
Generative engine optimization: making accurate, useful information easier for generative AI systems to understand and cite.
A content management system that stores and manages content separately from the front-end presentation layer.
Policies and systems used to identify users and control which resources and actions they are permitted to access.
A connection between systems that allows them to exchange data or coordinate actions.
A branch of AI in which models learn patterns from examples or data to support predictions, classifications, or other tasks.
Information that describes other information, such as a page title, image description, publication date, or data field.
Minimum viable product: a focused initial version that tests the core value of a product with the smallest practical feature set.
A development approach that uses visual tools and configuration to build applications or workflows with little or no hand-written code.
A standard authorization framework that allows an application to access permitted resources without receiving the user's password.
An approach to interface design that adapts layout and interaction to different screen sizes and device contexts.
Search engine optimization: improving technical accessibility, content relevance, and site structure to help search engines understand pages.
A standardized way of describing information on a page so search engines and other software can interpret its meaning.
An event-triggered message sent by one system to another when a specified action or change occurs.
A defined sequence of tasks, decisions, and handoffs used to complete a process.
A security approach that checks access explicitly and does not automatically trust a user or device solely because it is inside a network.
A configured attempt to resend an event notification after a delivery failure, usually with limits and backoff to avoid repeated load.
